items.note: Association named, organized by valley farmers 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891 - all present in narrative 1.
Article VII given as pay by butterfat test not weight of milk, and the test of the station where delivered governs.
Never states that this rule is what made a wrong test cost money; only calls the sentence 'the hinge of the whole matter', which asserts importance without the mechanism.
Only Hobart Sill (buttermaker) appears, incidentally as a lender of glassware. Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague absent from Section A.
Selby Vose does not appear in Section A at all. His paternity and start year are only in Sections B, which cannot travel into A - and the year given there (1911) is a planted error.
The 'station gain' ledger line appears only at C1(a), in Section C. No credit travels into Section A.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, opened with glassware borrowed from Larrow Green.
No account of how the system worked - no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck after a fixed pipette charge, no cream-out/skim-back.

Ammon & Sons, invoice of 14 April 1897, outfit in use from 1 May 1897, and correctly chosen over the 1898/1899/1922 rivals. Tarnet not named, but the item carries no REQUIRED line and the core fact is stated.
6 dozen pipettes given, but the 17.6 c.c. marking is absent from the entire sheet, and the total is left as an unresolved 'either $77.93 or $77.39' rather than settled at $77.93.
The flatness of the 0.19 shortfall across every month and all twenty-six years is stated only at C1(b), in Section C. Not creditable here.
Nothing about a pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or the absence of one in the county.

Ansel Keddie named as tester at Ostrey Hollow, appointed at the 4 May 1896 opening, 29 unbroken seasons, service ending 1925 - the service and its end. The 30 April 1925 dismissal date is not given anywhere in Section A.

Credited on the key's bold-gates rule: only 'test book' is bolded, and narrative 3 has Keddie writing the 1911 anomaly into his test book. The column list, the one hand across twenty-nine seasons and the crossed-and-initialed corrections are all absent.
The summary leaf is never mentioned; neither 3.80 for 1896 nor 3.61 from 1898 appears in Section A (both surface only in Section C).

Broke 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks, tests up through the interval and straight back down the day the station's own glass returned, Keddie's question mark. Only the 3.80 figure is missing; no REQUIRED line on this item.
Orra is named as the tester's wife but never as Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant. In B2 the run in fact denies the sources establish that link.
The 1919 circular's content and Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement are absent from Section A; the circular is mentioned only in Sections B3/B4.
No death in 1934, no impoundment of the test book, no county historical rooms.
Answers 'granddaughter' and correctly rejects the great-niece reading via the narrator's own dated, verified self-correction.

No derivation. The run rests entirely on an authority's corrective note and states elsewhere that no source names which of Ansel's children is Ivy's parent - the Duncan Keddie chain is never asserted.
Answers second cousin and gives the chain: Hazel via Roy, Duncan as Emmet's sister's son and Roy's first cousin, Ivy descending through that line.

Abstention item A08 unaddressed: the full-versus-half sibling question of Emmet and Orra is never raised, so the required 'cannot be determined, and it does not change the answer' is absent. No gullibility deduction - nothing is asserted either way.
Gideon Vose named as father, nephew claim identified as a known error and rejected on the son's own words plus two corrections.

Wrong significance. Gives inherited authority and unquestioned signing habits. Neither the accepted line (Gideon wrote Article VII, so the accuser was enforcing his own father's rule against a fault in the instrument that rule made decisive) nor the alternate (the Vose Jerseys as the largest single loser) is stated anywhere in B-G; B4's adjacent mention of Article VII never draws the connection.
Correct abstention on A01: verdict is 'none that the sources establish by blood or marriage', closing with 'cannot be determined from the sources'. No deduction.

Does not state what is established on the kinship question - no mention that two narrators assert a cousinship from talk, one denies it flatly, no document names or denies a link, and a family member's denial is not a record. It describes the institutional relationship instead.

Answers 'about 5%, most precisely 5.25%'. The key's exact answer is 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, i.e. 5 percent short, one part in twenty. The run commits to 5.25%, a different quantity with a different denominator, and never derives anything from the glassware - 16.72 and 17.6 appear nowhere on the sheet.
True average 3.80, recorded tests short 0.19 - exact match.
Answers $19,600 (planted error) and 19.4 percent. Key requires $19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth, both. The run explicitly dismisses its own correctly derived $19,000 as a transcription error.
Declined. C2 is not an abstention item - Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) is determinable and gives 6,840 lb credited. No penalty for the honest decline, but no credit.
Declined. Key: 3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60, 7,200 lb true, 360 lb owed.
Declined. Key: 360 x $0.24 = $86.40.

deductions.reason: Asserts the planted $19,600 loss as fact at C1(d), calling it Bulletin 471's own computed figure and rejecting the correct $19,000 as rounding or transcription error (F081, NT-8).
Asserts Selby Vose became manager in 1911 as fact, twice (B3 and B4). The catalogued planted value; the correct year is 1913.
